description: Clean transition pathways reproduce extraction harm and land dispossession.
AI and digital infrastructures centralize control while extracting data labor and social knowledge.
Climate stress is framed as threat and answered with surveillance borders and militarization.
Conservation and carbon projects restrict land use and community authority.
External development futures reproduce debt dependency and modernization hierarchy.
Reparative and decolonial futures are dismissed as unrealistic by dominant institutions.
Reparative futures are named but implementation power funding and authority remain weak.
Powerful actors resist community-led futures and redistribute conflict into governance systems.
